run1.title: Baseline
run1.lesson: Left to itself, gradient descent finds a slow fade instead of a reset, and a write gate that records time rather than distance. Both work a little at 10 seconds and not at all at 20. The memory was in F, but leaky.

run2.title: Erase penalty times ten
run2.lesson: Charging more for erasing away from food did not push the gate toward food; it shut the gate everywhere. With no erase at all, the tallies filled to the ceiling within a trip and the brain could not home. A scalar gate cannot be penalised into firing on five ticks out of three hundred.

run3.title: Two seconds at food
run3.lesson: Four times more food ticks did not teach the reset either, but it rebalanced the whole trip: a lower write gate, tallies off the ceiling, and, for the first time, a write gate that follows speed (+0.94). First brain to home on 20-second trips. Memory in F by a wide margin: 1.99 with it, 4.75 without.

run4.title: Five trips per episode
run4.lesson: More trips in a row did not make the erase gate fire at food (0.0045 at food, 0.0085 away: it erases LESS at food than elsewhere). The fade simply absorbed the dirty board, and the extra trips only cost score: 2.30 at 20 s against run 3's 1.90. Prediction failed. It did give the first 30-second numbers: 2.37 with F, 5.80 without, on trips it never trained at, so the memory generalises to longer wanders.

run5.title: Erase penalty ×10, warm start
run5.lesson: The penalty did nothing to the erase gate, because at 0.5 times a gate of 0.01 it adds 0.005 to a loss of about 2: a rounding error. Run 2 had died for cold-start reasons, not because the penalty was strong. What run 5 did show is the danger of long training near the ceiling: after a good stretch (best frozen exam 1.41 at iteration 400) it collapsed twice, and the second time it did not recover; the final network is worse than a random walk. Its best checkpoint ties run 4 at 30 s (2.37). Lesson: the optimiser needs a schedule that shrinks its steps late in a run.

run6.title: Stretch to 30 s, with cosine decay
run6.lesson: Trained at 30 seconds for the first time. By iteration 400 its frozen exam at 30 s was 1.77, far under the untrained 2.37, with the memory in F (5.48 without). Then the familiar collapse at 500 (write gate 0.38 to 0.64, loss to 12) and it did not recover by 600, so it was killed. Cosine decay alone was not enough: at iteration 500 of 1,200 the rate was still two thirds of full. Restarted as run 6B from the 1.77 checkpoint at a third of the base rate. Note: this stage was started on run 5's 64-trip frozen exam of 1.41, not on the running-score rule (which no run had met); see the narrative.

run6B.title: Run 6 restarted at a third of the learning rate
run6B.lesson: No collapse in 800 iterations at 30 seconds. Final network: 2.13 at 30 s with F, 5.91 without (22% arrived); 1.85 at 20 s. The lower rate is the fix for the late collapses: from here every warm start trains at 3e-4. The score has plateaued around 2.1 at 30 s, well above the 0.75 floor. Still a fade (0.005 at food, 0.009 away), write~speed +0.53, tallies saturated a third of the time at 30 s: the three things that still separate it from the fly.

run7.title: Erase penalty 20, warm
run7.lesson: Even a real penalty barely moved the gate: away-from-food erase went 0.0081 to 0.0075 in 200 iterations, and at-food erase fell rather than rose. The diagnosis is structural. The erase gate is a sigmoid whose bias sits near -5, where the curve is almost flat: its slope there is about 0.007, so every gradient reaching the gate, penalty or benefit, is multiplied by 0.007 before it can move anything. The gate is not refusing to learn the reset; it cannot hear the signal. Killed at 200; the fix is tested as run 7B.

run7B.title: Erase gate given a voice (bias +2.5)
run7B.lesson: The first run in which the erase gate prefers food. On the 200-trip test it erases 0.027 per tick at food against 0.009 away, a ratio of 3, with peaks of 0.06 at food; every earlier run was at or below 1. The ratio grew through training (1.1 at iteration 200, 1.5 at 700). It is a leaning, not yet a reset: the fly-like target is near 1 at food and near 0 away. The strong starting fade cost score, 2.55 at 30 s against the parent's 2.13, and 800 iterations were not enough to recover it. Prediction partly met: away-from-food erase did fall below 0.01; at-food erase reached 0.027 mean, short of 0.05; score did not recover.
